**Wave-2 tie-in (findings F2, F9, F12) — the context recommendation was Drew's own, and this design has a hard dependency.**

- **F2 — settled starting point.** The brief says "a context object was the recommendation that landed in some technical discussions." The recommendation was Drew's, 2026-10-07 (OpenCode session `ses_ef03b7d73ffewFUtEk0FCMTiz5`): capabilities as "server side dll that the program expects to be available… derived capabilities by looking at usage… extra classes/functions stored In context map or something so that the interface to compile against is semi stable." Cite that as the starting point; the unbuilt halves this design scopes are derivation-from-usage and user-function passing, not the context/catalogue direction itself (already chosen, already partly built as the `world_caps.rs` ceiling).
- **F9 — hard constraint.** Worlds accepting functions from users must respect the delegation semantics settled 2026-10-29 and built in `pkgs/id/src/groups/delegation.rs`: attenuation never amplifies, revoke cascades by reachability, and **no function values inside the replicated causal log** (resolution pre-emission only).
- **F12 — dependency, confirmed zero.** This design's client-side half depends on [#789](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/789) client-side capability providers, which Lane A confirmed on 2026-11-04 have **zero implementation today** (`CapabilityProvider` grep over `pkgs/id/src` returns nothing; #789 sits on the program's zero-implementation list). Design homes for that dependency: [#5686](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5686) and [#5931](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5931) — this design files under them, not as a parallel effort.

Record: `workspace/scratch/worlds-capabilities-brief-2026-11-04/conversation-tie-ins.md` (F2, F9, F12).

**Wave-2 follow-ups filed from the prior-art research (Lane B).** Granular sub-scopes of this issue, each carrying the relevant research findings + citations:

- [id: research: effect-language borrowings — which Koka/Unison properties to emulate in id tooling, which to skip](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5997)

Research source: `workspace/scratch/worlds-capabilities-brief-2026-11-04/prior-art-research.md`. Full wave-2 mapping: `workspace/scratch/worlds-capabilities-brief-2026-11-04/wave2-map.md`.

Link from the #5997 spec note (filed as a wave-2 child of this topic): the effect-language borrowings note has landed — [`doc/2026-11-05_design_id5997.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-05_design_id5997.md), merged via PR #6327 (merge `cfabb25fccbf`).

Decisions recorded there that bear on this programming-model topic (details and costs in the note, §7):

- **Effect-row inference (Koka): approximate** — used-capability sets are derived by call-graph reachability over the closed platform-function namespace, not by type-level rows.
- **Ability-checked signatures (Unison): emulate the check, approximate the signature** — declared ceiling in tooling metadata, derived used-set must be a subset, checked at compile/admission time, failing closed.
- **Content-addressed definitions (Unison): emulate at the identity layer** — continuous with the #5965 compile-cache key.
- **OCaml-style untyped effects: skip** — standing constraint: capability failures must be discoverable at compile/admission time, never first at runtime.
- **Zig-style explicit context structs: keep as the mechanism** — derivation/checking is an audit layer over explicit passing (`context.platform.fn`), never a replacement for it.

## Queue triage — task 10332 (2026-11-05)

**Fresh state:** #5963 remains OPEN on current `main` (`c8a1913bd338da1601fd3aa68187757f5a9087da`). No hard-stop labels and no PR directly implementing this issue. PR [#6327](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/6327) is merged, but it implements the separate #5997 spec note; it does not satisfy #5963. The #5997 note is now available at [`doc/2026-11-05_design_id5997.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-05_design_id5997.md).

**Route:** keep this as design work, not a bug fix. The repo baseline includes pure helpers with app-owned state in [`RocCap.roc`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/pkgs/id/examples/roc-world/RocCap.roc), but it does not yet demonstrate the platform/context-passing convention this issue must choose. Use #5997 as settled input: platform capabilities remain explicitly passed as context values (`context.platform.fn`); used-capability derivation is a compile-time call-graph approximation over the closed platform namespace; declared ceilings are checked against derived usage at compile/admission time and fail closed. Do not reopen ambient/runtime-discovered authority or hand-maintained used sets.

The #5963 design doc should now decide: context-record vs explicit-parameter ergonomics and granularity; how a library signature/metadata exposes its required surface to the #5956 import checker; platform-context versioning; and how user-passed functions fit the same boundary. Preserve the function-delegation constraints already recorded above (attenuation only, revocation by reachability, function values resolved before emission and never placed in the replicated causal log).

**Ordering / dependencies:** coordinate the signature/import boundary with open #5956 and the ceiling vocabulary with open #5958. Keep #5998 as the follow-up that owns the derivation/checker design and implementation; #5963 can define the source-level contract without waiting for its implementation. The open provider-model work (#5686/#5931) informs provider-facing compatibility but is not a blocker to selecting the core library-passing convention; #789 and #2028 being closed does not close this newer scope.

No implementation or test run is expected from this triage.

## Decision summary — programming model design (#5963)

Design record: [`2026-11-08T17-23-00Z_design_id5963_programming_model.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/queue/12864-5963-platform-context-design/doc/2026-11-08T17-23-00Z_design_id5963_programming_model/2026-11-08T17-23-00Z_design_id5963_programming_model.md), proposed in [PR #7768](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7768).

- **Passing and granularity:** one explicit Roc `context` value; its `platform` member is a typed, nested record, projected per library to only the required operation leaves under each domain. Do not pass the whole platform. Independent function arguments are not the general library convention.
- **Import contract:** the exported context type is the source contract; versioned `platform.requires` metadata is its generated machine-readable view, unioned with transitive package requirements. The import gate checks `requires(L) ⊆ world.effective_grant`; #5998's statically `discovered_used` set remains distinct and must be certified within the declared surface. The exact manifest wire format/checker remains with #5956/#5998.
- **Versioning:** pin each world build to #5958's vocabulary/catalog identity and profile. Capability additions or semantic changes require explicit rebuild/re-check; no silent widening. The record aligns to the current #5958 proposal in open PR #7599 rather than introducing a parallel vocabulary.
- **User functions:** attenuation only; revocation follows reachability; resolve a permitted function before emission; never place function values/closures in the replicated causal log.

The design uses #5997's settled `context.platform.fn` direction and compile/admission-time fail-closed checks. `RocCap.roc` is cited as a pure Roc/state-passing data point, not as an existing platform-context example. This is design-only; no implementation was started.

## Resume findings — PR #7768 design review

The independent read-only review found one blocking contract gap and one link correction. This task remains parked; no follow-up code edit has been made in this launch.

- **Blocking:** the record must prohibit library source from bypassing its projected `context` with direct `pf.*` platform-module imports. The current `world_compile.rs::check_imports` gate checks imports against world grants, which alone does not enforce the per-library projection. Require all library platform access to use the explicit context boundary (with direct platform imports limited to the core adapter that constructs projections), or define equivalent package-level enforcement under #5956.
- **Nonblocking:** both relative links to the #5997 note use one too many `../` segments; change `../../2026-11-05_design_id5997.md` to `../2026-11-05_design_id5997.md`.

Decision summary:
- Mechanism: one explicit context value; context.platform is a typed record of named capabilities (context.platform.<domain>.<operation>). Whole-platform passing, per-capability argument lists, unstructured maps, and ambient/runtime discovery all rejected with reasons.
